messages:
sara_cs: Hey team — ACME flagged a regression after yesterday's model rollout. They say a billing-summary prompt that used to return a concise line-item breakdown now returns hallucinated fields and repeats. They attached request id r-8f3b2 and example prompt/output.

acme_prod: @sara_cs here's the example: prompt -> `Summarize charges for invoice #INV-9932`. Response now: 
```
Total: $1,234.56\nLine items: Consulting x 3, Misc fees x 2, UnknownCharge x 999\nNote: previous balance carried: $12,345.67\n```
This used to be tidy and only list the invoice items. We saw this immediately after the 19:00 deploy.

sara_cs: Thanks — filing and pinging eng/ML. Mike can you check model version and canary status?

mike_ml: Looking. Canary rollout for v2.14 started at 18:45, 30% traffic. Internal evals (billing-regress-suite v2) pass: accuracy 98.7%, hallucination rate <0.5%. The request id maps to model shard `redwood-billing-v2.14-quant32`.

anya_eng: Devops-bot shows a gradual increase in `prompt_len` for ACME around that time and some autosplit behavior from the request router. Not sure if that's related. Devops-bot: canary=30% -> 60% at 18:58 due to traffic surge (auto-burst). :eyes:
devops-bot: deployment note: rollout v2.14 -> traffic bumped to 60% at 18:58 for region us-west-2 (auto-burst).

mike_ml: Hmm. Two hypotheses: (1) the quantized kernel for v2.14 interacts badly with certain numeric tokenization patterns ACME uses, leading to token merging and hallucinated numerics; (2) prefix-caching + batching with autosplit caused partial context truncation so model guesses missing items.

joel_pm: Customer wants a hotfix or rollback. Can we reproduce internally with their prompt? If internal evals pass, there's an eval mismatch we need to narrow down.

sara_cs: I asked ACME for full request payload (they sent obfuscated customer ids). They included `max_tokens: 256`, `temperature: 0.0`, `system` prompt: "Extract invoice items only" and the user prompt.

mike_ml: Reproduced locally against v2.14 with exact payload and tokenization settings — I see the hallucinated `UnknownCharge` when `lead_zero_padding` tokens appear in ACME's dataset (they pad invoice numbers with leading zeros). With a synthetic example: 
```
prompt: "Invoice 00009932 \nList items"
model=v2.14
response: contains 'UnknownCharge x 999'
```

anya_eng: Did we run that same sample in the billing-regress-suite? Maybe the test corpus doesn't have lead-zero invoice numbers.

mike_ml: Correct — our test set had mixed numeric formats but not the repeated zero-padding pattern. So internal evals missed this edge case. That explains the mismatch.

joel_pm: OK — plan? Rollback v2.14 for ACME tenant or push a hotfix? ACME is on Dedicated but uses hosted control plane; they asked for rollback to v2.13.

sara_cs: ACME requested rollback ASAP. They're on a production-critical flow. I can offer a temporary routing to v2.13 for their org id if we can do it quickly.

anya_eng: We can add a tenant routing override to send acme_org -> v2.13. I'll need a short config change and a deploy window. devops-bot: create routing change?
devops-bot: routing-change ticket created: R-4021 assigned to anya_eng. ETA 20 minutes for traffic switch, change will be logged and can be reverted.

mike_ml: Meanwhile I'll prepare a deterministic unit test with zero-padded invoice numbers and add it to billing-regress-suite. Also testing two mitigations: (A) normalization preprocessor that strips leading zeros from invoice IDs for parsing tasks; (B) a small prompt-fix that enforces item format. Early local runs: preprocessor removes hallucination.

joel_pm: Good. Sara please propose the routing rollback to ACME and give ETA. Also log the regression as a sev-2 with product impact and include the reproducer + test case.

sara_cs: Message to ACME: "We see the issue and will route you to v2.13 within ~20 minutes while we roll a fix. We'll follow up with a permanent patch and a test update." Sent. They replied :relieved:.

mike_ml: Action items: 1) anya to apply tenant routing override (R-4021) — confirmed in 20m. 2) mike to add zero-pad test to suite and instrument tokenization differences. 3) dev to evaluate preprocessor vs prompt-fix; decide which goes to canary. 4) joel to create incident ticket and coordinate customer comms.

anya_eng: Routing change applied at 18:58:45 -> ACME now on v2.13. Monitoring logs show their request r-8f3b2 reprocessed against v2.13 yields the expected concise itemized output.

acme_prod: Confirmed on our side: responses back to normal. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

mike_ml: I'll cut a hotfix branch with the preprocessor and run it through an internal smoke canary (10% traffic). If stable, we'll include it in next patch and expand canary slowly.

joel_pm: Thanks team. Let's keep the thread for postmortem notes — we need to update the billing-regress-suite and add specific tokenization cases to avoid eval mismatch in future. :memo:
